plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies, so rational opponents anticipating my behavior doesn't change this optimal strategy. My value is $15, so I bid exactly $15.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of other bidders' strategies or beliefs, because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $36, I will bid exactly that to maximize expected profit, as this strategy is optimal regardless of what Andy and Charles do.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds even with rational opponents trying to anticipate my behavior - truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit because I win exactly when my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay only that second-highest bid. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. My value is $42, so I will bid $42.
